The covariant derivatives of the nonlinear representation of the group are obtained by using the global and infinitesimal considerations of the representation manifold.

(1) the nonlinear representation manifold of a given compact group is a Riemannian space with the metric given by the Killing form of the group, and (2) the nonlinear covariant derivative is given by the Christoffel symbol of the metric.

(1) the covariant derivative is the key concept for constructing invariant Lagrangians, (2) the global and infinitesimal approaches to constructing invariant Lagrangian densities are related, (3) the noncompact case is treated in a straightforward fashion, (4) the zero mass problem can be resolved in some cases, and (5) the possibility of embedding in a higher dimensional space is a general feature of nonlinear representations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of determining arbitrary non‐linear representations of a given Lie group.
a systematic study of arbitrary nonlinear representations of compact groups, and the problem of constructing Lagrangian fields invariant under these representations.
the problem of constructing Lagrangian fields invariant under a given compact Lie Group.

the nonlinear chiral transformations of a given group G are determined by the requirement that the covariant derivative of any tensor field be an element of the algebra of G.

it provides a unified treatment of the problem, and that it is possible to construct nonlinear representations of a compact group by means of an appropriate embedding of a representation manifold in a larger space.

the problem of constructing a Lagrangian invariant under a given group is equivalent to the problem of determining the covariant derivatives.

the nonlinearity of the representation is not an obstruction to the construction of a Lagrangian invariant under the group.

it is possible to construct a nonlinear representation by solving an appropriate set of equations for the coefficients in the expansion of the representation in terms of the generators of the Lie algebra.
